evidence.claim: External evidence describes AI infrastructure bottlenecks moving beyond semiconductors into physical infrastructure such as cooling, power semiconductors, and data-center energy solutions, while also flagging chemicals such as sulphuric acid and naphtha as obscure semiconductor manufacturing constraints.
evidence.source_title: Running Hot Into Scarcity: Why Bottlenecks Are the Risk to the AI “Bubble”

evidence.claim: External evidence frames long-term AI exposure as shifting from overextended chip makers toward the physical infrastructure layer, specifically cooling, power semiconductors, and data-center energy solutions.
evidence.source_title: Running Hot Into Scarcity: Why Bottlenecks Are the Risk to the AI “Bubble”

evidence.claim: External evidence states that AI-server MLCC bottlenecks are concentrated in high-end parts requiring small size, high capacitance, low ESR, and low ESL, supporting the broader claim that AI infrastructure bottlenecks can appear in obscure components rather than only GPUs or HBM.
evidence.source_title: Murata: The Stock You Missed If You Only Bought GPUs and HBM in the AI Rally

evidence.claim: External evidence reports Powell Industries fiscal 2026 second-quarter revenue of about $296.6 million, new orders of about $490 million, book-to-bill of 1.7x, backlog of about $1.8 billion, and a data-center mega-order valued above $400 million after quarter close.
evidence.source_title: Everyone Is Chasing AI Chips. We're Looking for the Bottlenecks.

evidence.claim: Powell's reported backlog growth and large data-center order suggest AI infrastructure spending may be flowing into electrical-equipment suppliers such as switchgear, power control rooms, and engineered power systems.
evidence.source_title: Everyone Is Chasing AI Chips. We're Looking for the Bottlenecks.

evidence.claim: The Powell evidence is not direct evidence for VRT, ETN, GEV, NVT, or ATKR, but it raises the prior that AI data-center capex is reaching electrical infrastructure and balance-of-plant suppliers; ticker-level validation remains required.
evidence.source_title: Everyone Is Chasing AI Chips. We're Looking for the Bottlenecks.

evidence.claim: External evidence cites optical interconnects as one of the AI infrastructure areas that has received market attention alongside GPUs and HBM, supporting optical networking as a relevant supply-chain lane to map.
evidence.source_title: Murata: The Stock You Missed If You Only Bought GPUs and HBM in the AI Rally

memory_update.text: LITE mapped to AI optical-networking component chain as an underfollowed inference; direct evidence needed on datacom mix, 800G/1.6T, AI customers, margins, and capacity.
COHR mapped to AI optical-networking photonics/materials chain as an underfollowed inference; direct evidence needed on AI datacenter revenue, InP/laser constraints, and margin mix.
FN mapped to optical manufacturing and precision assembly as an underfollowed hypothesis; validate datacom/AI module revenue, customer concentration, capacity utilization, and dual-sourcing risk.
AAOI remains speculative_shadow for data-center transceivers; must verify named customer wins, 800G/1.6T qualification, gross margins, and balance-sheet durability.
POET remains speculative_shadow for co-packaged optics and optical engines; require proof of commercial shipments, qualifications, manufacturing partnerships, and cash runway.
VRT is a reference leader for AI data-center power and cooling infrastructure; monitor backlog, liquid cooling, AI datacenter mix, and margin sustainability.
ETN is a reference leader for data-center electrical equipment and power management; use as a benchmark for switchgear, backlog, lead times, and pricing.
GEV is a reference leader for power-generation and grid bottlenecks tied to AI data-center power availability; validate turbine/grid backlog and data-center relevance.
NVT mapped as an underfollowed data-center electrical balance-of-plant hypothesis; verify data-center mix, product criticality, lead times, order growth, and pricing.
ATKR mapped as an underfollowed second-order data-center construction input hypothesis; verify data-center mix and whether raceway/conduit demand has pricing power or is commoditized.
Optical-networking candidates in this chunk lack primary-source evidence tying revenue or backlog directly to AI clusters, 800G/1.6T deployments, hyperscaler qualifications, or capacity bottlenecks.
Electrical-infrastructure candidates beyond Powell require company-level primary evidence for data-center order growth, backlog duration, lead times, pricing, and AI-specific end-market exposure.
Balance-of-plant names NVT and ATKR may be obscure second-order beneficiaries, but they need product criticality and margin evidence before promotion in the Serenity funnel.

summary: Layer 2B maps the candidate chunk into two relationship lanes: (1) AI optical-networking subsupply, where LITE, COHR, FN, AAOI, and POET may sit beneath GPU/networking leaders as lasers, photonics, optical-module manufacturing, or speculative optical-engine suppliers; and (2) AI data-center physical infrastructure, where VRT, ETN, GEV are reference leaders and NVT/ATKR are underfollowed balance-of-plant candidates. Evidence quality is strongest for the broad AI-infrastructure bottleneck thesis and for Powell-style electrical backlog precedent from cached Layer 2A, but weaker for direct company-level exposure in this chunk. Most underfollowed tickers should remain in evidence-needed status until filings, segment disclosures, customer references, backlog/order data, and margin drivers confirm AI-specific materiality. This is research support only, not a recommendation.
